subject: Re: Eval plan & next steps for AcmeFin model fit
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Bennett <sam.bennett@acmefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps: AcmeFin eval plan

Hi Sam / Priya,

Really appreciate the time today - great convo on your fraud-detection summarization and triage use case. Recap of what we discussed and recommended next steps so we have a shared plan:

Summary of fit / recommendation
- Primary goals: improve triage summaries for analyst review, reduce false positives in automated labeling, and keep latency under 250ms for single-shot inference.
- Initial model candidates we recommend trying on Redwood:
  1) Llama-2-70B-Chat (quantized float16/8) - strong instruction-following and higher-quality long-form summarization.
  2) Mistral-Instruct (13B) - cost-efficient, good for short summarization and reranking.
  3) Mosaic MPT-7B-Instruct (7B) - latency/cost baseline for edge-case comparisons.

Suggested eval plan (what we can run on Redwood)
- Dataset: customer-provided sample of 1,200 labeled events (see attached preview). Preferred format: JSONL with fields: id, prompt, expected_response, metadata (source_system, label, priority). See attachment acmefin_eval_prompt_set_v1.jsonl.
- Scoring criteria:
  - Primary: semantic similarity using embeddings (cosine similarity) for free-text summaries (thresholds we can tune, start at 0.85).
  - Secondary: token-level accuracy for structured label extraction (exact match / normalized).
  - Aggregate: weighted score (0.6 semantic similarity, 0.4 structured exact-match) and pass threshold 0.75.
- Sample size: recommend 1,000-2,000 examples for statistically meaningful results; start with the 1,200 you mentioned.

Benchmarking & artifacts
- I uploaded a short benchmarks doc with baseline numbers for the three models (latency, cost per 1k tokens, and dev-time prompts). Link in the attachments and Drive.
- Prompt sets: included a small curated prompt suite for triage summary prompts plus failure cases (edge prompts).

Operational notes for running on Redwood
- How we run: you can upload the JSONL to the Drive link (or provide S3) and we'll create an eval job in Redwood that runs each model variant, returns per-example scores, and produces a summary report with failure cases.
- We recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated prompts and a batch size that keeps P99 latency under your 250ms SLO. Our engineer will advise exact batching after we see token-length distribution.

Next steps / asks (proposed timeline)
1) You: share the full dataset (JSONL) and a short privacy/data note for security review by EOD Thu.
2) We (Redwood): spin up eval job, run the three recommended models, and send a preliminary results deck within 3 business days of data receipt.
3) Joint review call to go over results and rollout recommendations (can be 30-45 minutes).

Attachments: acmefin_eval_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, acmefin_benchmark_links.md, acmefin_sample_dataset_preview.csv

If that plan looks right I'll request the security checklist and schedule the eval job.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0132

[Attachment: acmefin_eval_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (application/jsonl)]
[Attachment: acmefin_benchmark_links.md (text/markdown)]

From: Sam Bennett <sam.bennett@acmefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acmefin.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps: AcmeFin eval plan

Thanks Marissa - this is super helpful and aligns with what we need. A couple quick clarifications before we share the full dataset:

1) Scoring: for the semantic similarity metric, when you say embeddings cosine >= 0.85, is that comparing model output to a human-written gold summary? Are you using Redwood embeddings or do you recommend an external embedding model?
2) Dataset PII: some of our events contain masked account IDs and transaction hashes. Do you need anything else in the metadata to keep traceability for our analysts?

We can share the full JSONL by EOD Thu. Also looping in our security ops (security@acmefin.com) to confirm the checklist.

Thanks,
Sam

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acmefin.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps: AcmeFin eval plan

Hi Sam - quick answers:

1) Embeddings: we default to Redwood-ephemeral-embed-001 for consistency across runs (we can also support your preferred embedding model if you have a governance requirement). The cosine >= 0.85 threshold is a starting point comparing model output against a human-written gold summary. We'll surface per-example embeddings and similarity so you can adjust thresholds.

2) PII/traceability: masked IDs are fine. Please include a stable id field and source_system in metadata so we can trace any failing examples back to your dataset. Don't put raw PII in the expected_response field - masked or tokenized values are preferred.

Logistics: once you upload the JSONL to the Drive link (or provide an S3 URL), Neha will kick off the eval run and I'll monitor. We'll include a results sheet with example-level diffs, aggregate metrics, and recommended model variant (quantization tradeoffs included).

Proposed timeslot for joint review call next week: Thu 3/25 10:00-10:45 PT or Fri 3/26 9:00-9:45 PT - which works for you?

Thanks!
Marissa
